blocks.title: The One True Limit
blocks.text: Everything Git tracks is recoverable except working-tree changes that were never added and never committed. That is the only point of no return.

caption.text: Part 2 of GIT UNDO: THE FIELD MANUAL. "I lost my commits with reset --hard" is almost always false — the commits are still sitting in your reflog. This field manual walks every undo Git gives you: the three trees underneath them all, reset's three depths, revert for anything already pushed, restore, stash, and fsck rescues for work you thought was gone. Save it for the day your stomach drops.
